# Retired- and static-instruction baselines for the bench corpus,
# checked against every run by scripts/ci-check-perf.
#
# FORMAT: metric  value  [tolerance%]. The metric key is
# <arch>/<benchmark>.<text|ir> — .text is the count of instructions in the
# emitted assembly, .ir the count of instructions actually retired.
#
# WHAT IS EXACT AND WHAT IS NOT. Every figure here repeats to the digit on a
# given commit EXCEPT the rows that hash string keys: core/map draws a
# per-process string-hash seed (#6194), which moves probe lengths, so a
# benchmark that builds a string-keyed map counts differently every run. That
# is `map_string.ir`, measured at a 0.541% spread over 15 runs of one binary;
# it keeps the 2% it was given for a 0.51% spread, on BOTH arches, since the
# seed is drawn per process and not per ISA. A range grows with sample count,
# so this is a floor, not a ceiling — do not tighten a tolerance here against a
# handful of runs. The `utf8_ingest_*.ir` rows hashed their keys the same way
# through json_parse until an object stopped being a Map; its objects are under
# the size that builds a key index, so they are exact now. Absolute endpoints are
# deliberately NOT quoted: they go stale the next time a line is re-banked for
# an unrelated reason, and a stale range reads as a real one. `map_int.ir` is
# exact — the seed is consulted for string keys only — and is deliberately
# left on the default so the two together show which half of a map regression
# moved.
#
# Everything else uses the 1% default, which flags a change of one part in a
# hundred. That is a significance threshold and not a noise floor: for those
# rows the count is exact, which `int_loop.ir` measuring identically over six
# runs is the control for.
#
# STRICT, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — perf.yml runs this comparison with
# FERN_CI_PERF_GATE_STRICT=1, so a row outside its tolerance fails the job
# whether it got worse or better. When a number moves on purpose, update it in
# the same PR; the job summary prints the corrected lines ready to paste. Keep
# the reason in the PR, not here.
#
# TWO ARCHITECTURES. An instruction count is not comparable across ISAs, so the
# keys are namespaced by arch and compared independently — and each job compares
# only its OWN namespace, so an x86_64 entry is not a missing measurement on the
# aarch64 runner.

# Re-pinned 2026-10-11 (#12117) on seven x86_64 and six aarch64 rows after a
# carried reuse donor's token is taken where the donor dies and a split
# read's part phi is shared by every read: the `.text` rows fell 1-4% on both
# (http_hello -3.6%, perceus_cfold -3.3%, pmap_insert -2.3% and -1.8%,
# pvec_with -2.0% and -2.2%, ordmap_insert -1.3% and -1.6%); pmap_insert.ir
# fell 3.9% on x86_64 and ordmap_insert.ir 5.5% on aarch64, while
# ordmap_insert.ir rose 1.2% on x86_64, the token taken at each arm's exit
# with its uniqueness test and children drop there, where the construction
# past the join tested it once. Values are the perf-x86_64 and perf-aarch64
# lanes' measurements of the branch.

# Re-pinned 2026-10-21 (#12921) after the sole-owner append kernel grew a full
# receiver in one frame: the `.text` rows carry the longer kernel, +51
# instructions on every x86_64 binary and +35 on aarch64 (eleven and nine
# rows past the tolerance), while the grows retire fewer instructions
# (struct_drop.ir -1.8% and -1.9%, sort_inplace.ir and
# utf8_ingest_validated.ir -1.1% on aarch64). Values are the perf-x86_64 and
# perf-aarch64 lanes' measurements of the branch.

# aarch64, the arch this project defaults to. The `.ir` half comes from the
# Perf workflow's own perf-aarch64 job, because no aarch64 host is available to
# the dev container — paste its block in verbatim. The `.text` half needs no
# such thing: it is a line count over `fern -target arm64-linux` output, which
# is host-independent, so a cross-compile from the dev container reproduces the
# runner's figure on EVERY row in this corpus and that is how the `.text` half
# is kept current. perf-aarch64 runs natively on ubuntu-24.04-arm, so the two
# are directly comparable. The seeded row, map_string.ir, carries the same
# tolerance its x86_64 twin does, for the same per-process hash seed, which is
# drawn per process rather than per ISA.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-09-04 (#7397) on the x86_64 `.text` half only, after the #4873
# containment bracket gained three field- and path-granular deaths: the three
# persistent-collection benchmarks lose bracket pairs (ordmap_insert -3.6%,
# pmap_insert -1.3%, pvec_with -1.2%). Every `.ir` row moved by less than its
# tolerance, so the trade is static size, not work.
#
# The two utf8_ingest `.text` rows were re-pinned in the same commit and
# credited to it. They are not its doing: the parent, a5cea3cd2, measures 31,424
# and 31,915 itself, so the +417 apiece was already on main. The values stand;
# the attribution did not. `map_int.text`, `map_string.text` and
# `map_probe_chain.ir` carry drift of the same kind — the last of them +1.35%,
# over its tolerance — and all three read identically at that parent, so they
# are left for whoever moved them rather than re-pinned here.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-09-05 (#8530) where the `.with` and constructor-reuse
# decisions moved into the IR: every row was measured twice on THIS corpus, on
# origin/main and on the change, and only the rows the pair disagreed on by
# more than their own tolerance were touched. Dynamically nothing got slower
# (pvec_with -10.5%, sort_inplace -7.8%, pmap_insert -5.9%); four `.text` rows
# grew 3-5%, which is the inline branch standing in for a call at every `.with`
# site. `array_with` and `record_update` are new, so their rows are first
# pins rather than re-pins — and their aarch64 `.ir` half is missing, because
# no aarch64 host measures it here; perf-aarch64 reports the two UNBASELINED
# for one run and its block goes in verbatim.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-11 (#12103) on the four utf8_ingest rows of each arch,
# whose json_parse now scans strings with __scan_set: `.ir` fell 19-29%
# (x86_64 unchecked -28.7%, validated -18.8%; aarch64 -26.4%, -18.4%) and
# `.text` grew 0.7-1.7% for the scan's tables and run helpers. Both figures
# for both arches are this branch's own measurement.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-12 (#12105 slice 4) on the four utf8_ingest rows of each
# arch, whose json_parse builds an object as two arrays instead of a Map
# (x86_64 `.ir` -16.5% unchecked, -8.9% validated; `.text` -23%), and on
# http_hello.text (+3.8%): std/http imports std/json, and the tree shaker keeps
# a method by bare name where a call's receiver is untyped, so JsonObject's
# `get` / `len` and its seeded key hash are kept. The aarch64 `.text` rows are
# cross-compiled readings; its `.ir` rows come from the perf-aarch64 lane.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-12 (#12262) on the four utf8_ingest rows of each arch,
# whose json_parse threads one position cell instead of a cursor (x86_64 `.ir`
# -9.7% unchecked, -5.1% validated; `.text` -15%), and on http_hello.text and
# pmap_insert.text (-5.8% and -0.9%): the tree shaker now keeps a method by its
# receiver's type wherever that type is known, not by its bare name. The
# aarch64 `.text` rows are cross-compiled readings; its `.ir` rows come from
# the perf-aarch64 lane.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-13 (#12331) on http_hello.text (x86_64 +3.7%, aarch64
# +4.1%): a produced body's trailers (+65 on x86_64), std/fetch driving an
# HTTP/2 connection (+163), and the inliner splicing a shared callee its
# caller reads apart whatever the caller's size (+471, the four splices it
# now admits: `__serve_event` twice, `__serve_park` and `fetch.idle` into the
# serve loop, `__chunked_trailers` into the request parser), which is what
# keeps the hello path at zero allocations. Both `.text` figures are this
# branch's own measurement, the aarch64 one cross-compiled and equal to the
# perf-aarch64 lane's reading.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-13 (#12344) on http_hello.ir (x86_64 -1.65%, aarch64
# -1.57%): the inliner splices a once-called callee that returns a box into
# a caller past its budget, so the serve loop no longer builds
# `__serve_pass_end`'s tuple on every pass. Both figures are the perf lanes'.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-14 (#12406) on sort_ints.ir, string_build.ir and
# struct_drop.ir (x86_64 +5.5%, +2.2%, +1.7%; aarch64 +3.8%, +1.7%, +1.3%):
# a branch between two pure values is now a conditional move, which runs
# both arms where the branch ran one. These rows' branches are predictable,
# so callgrind, which has no branch predictor, counts only the cost. Wall
# time on sort_ints scaled up is 5-10% faster; struct_drop's is within
# noise. Both arches' figures are the perf lanes'. The same change takes
# aarch64 ordmap_insert.text and sort_strings.text down 1.0% and 1.1%,
# measured by the perf-aarch64 lane. With #12402's constant index on top,
# x86_64 sort_inplace.text falls 1.1%; neither PR's own run saw the two
# together. The figure is the perf-x86_64 lane's.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-15 (#12418) on every row that moved: semreach drops code
# no reachable construction enables, so `.text` falls by up to 63% where a
# benchmark's imports carry what it never builds (array_scale_f64, sort_inplace,
# string_count_byte) and by 16% on http_hello. `.ir` moves less than 1.5% on
# every row. Rows moved a few tenths by earlier merges are re-banked to the same
# reading. x86_64 figures are the dev container's perf-bench run; the aarch64
# `.text` rows are cross-compiled readings, and its `.ir` rows are unchanged.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-17 (#12582) on x86_64/http_hello.text (+1.17%): the
# chunked-body join and the TLS record writer call __bytes_into, so the hello
# server carries its runtime helper where it inlined a byte loop. The figure is
# the perf-x86_64 lane's.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-18 (#12630) on http_hello.ir (x86_64 -9.73%, aarch64
# -8.54%): the request head is scanned once for its shape, the framing fields
# are found in one pass, the body deadline starts after the burst's parse, and
# the version prefix goes through the mismatch kernel. Both figures are the
# perf lanes' own.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-18 (#12644) on http_hello.text (x86_64 +2.93%, aarch64
# +3.23%): std/http's `__bytes_are` is the `__mismatch_bytes_str` kernel,
# inlined at its three callers, in place of a byte loop. `.ir` does not move:
# the benchmark parses without a previous request, so those compares never
# run there. Both figures are the perf lanes' own.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-18 (#12743, merged with the lane red) on both arches:
# core/int.int_to_string is a constant for 0 to 99, so every binary that
# formats an integer carries the table (`.text` +3% on http_hello, +7% on
# map_string, +17% to +33% on sort_strings, string_build, string_scan and
# struct_drop) and the ones that format small integers in their loop run
# fewer instructions (string_build.ir -26%, struct_drop.ir -35%,
# http_hello.ir -3%). Both arches' figures are the perf lanes' own.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-18 on x86_64/perceus_cfold.ir (-2.55%),
# perceus_deriv.text (-1.24%) and perceus_deriv.ir (-8.84%): a record whose
# fields are i64 or f64 constants, and an integer literal cast to its field's
# width, are static boxes, so the constant records those programs build on
# every round allocate nothing. The x86_64 figures are the dev container's
# perf-bench run; the aarch64 rows (perceus_cfold.ir -3.41%,
# perceus_deriv.text -1.68%, perceus_deriv.ir -8.93%) are the perf lane's.
#
# Re-pinned 2026-10-18 (#12781) on x86_64 ordmap_insert.ir (-1.83%),
# pmap_insert.ir (-2.72%) and pvec_with.ir (-3.50%), with their `.text` rows
# and http_hello.text (#12780, +0.22%): a payload read out of an enum held in
# an array slot or a local is taken rather than retained, so the node the
# update rebuilds is unique. The x86_64 figures are the dev container's
# perf-bench run; the aarch64 rows (ordmap_insert.ir -2.48%, pmap_insert.ir
# -2.81%, pvec_with.text -3.26%, pvec_with.ir -3.80%) are the perf lane's.
#
# Do NOT extrapolate an aarch64 figure from its x86_64 twin: the ratio is not
# constant. Over `.text` it runs from 0.85 (call_overhead) to 1.18
# (utf8_ingest_unchecked) — one ISA emitting fewer instructions than the other
# on one program says nothing about the next. A new benchmark reports as
# UNBASELINED here for one CI run, which is the gate saying "measured,
# recorded, not yet compared" — paste that run's block in rather than guessing.
